verses.text: These are more wise sayings of Solomon, which were copied down by the men of Hezekiah king of Judah.
It is God's glory to hide things, but it is the glory of kings to search things out.
As the sky is high and the earth is deep, so the hearts of kings cannot be understood.
Remove the waste from silver, and the silversmith can make something beautiful.
Remove the wicked from the king's presence, and his throne will be made secure by doing what is right.
Do not try to make yourself look important in front of the king. Do not claim a place among great people.
It is better to be told, "Come up here," than to be sent lower down in front of an important person you have seen.
Do not rush to take someone to court. What will you do in the end if your neighbour proves you wrong and puts you to shame?
If you have an argument with your neighbour, settle it between the two of you. Do not tell another person's secret,
or whoever hears it may shame you, and your bad name will never go away.
Words spoken at the right time are like golden apples in a silver setting.
Wise correction to a listening ear is like a gold earring or a necklace of fine gold.
A faithful messenger is like cool snow at harvest time to those who send him. He refreshes his masters.
Someone who boasts about gifts they never give is like clouds and wind that bring no rain.
A ruler can be persuaded by patience, and gentle words can break bones.
If you find honey, eat only as much as you need, or you will eat too much and throw it up.
Do not visit your neighbour's house too often, or they will get tired of you and hate you.
A person who tells lies about their neighbour in court is like a club, a sword, or a sharp arrow.
Trusting an unfaithful person in times of trouble is like having a bad tooth or a crippled foot.
Singing songs to someone with a heavy heart is like taking away their coat on a cold day, or pouring vinegar on soda.
If your enemy is hungry, give him food to eat. If he is thirsty, give him water to drink.
By doing this, you will heap burning coals on his head, and the LORD will reward you.
As the north wind brings rain, a gossiping tongue brings angry looks.
It is better to live in a corner on the roof than to share a house with a quarrelling wife.
Good news from a faraway land is like cold water to a thirsty person.
A good person who gives in to the wicked is like a muddy spring or a dirty well.
It is not good to eat too much honey, and it is not honourable to look for honour for yourself.
A person without self-control is like a city with broken-down walls.
